questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Slope of a Tangent Line of a Curve at a Given Point
questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=-2{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{(x-2{)}^{2}}.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=3$ is equal to ${f}^{′}(3).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{(x-2{)}^{2}}) \\  & =-4x+(-2(x-2{)}^{-3}) \\  & =-4x-\frac{2}{(x-2{)}^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=3$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(3) & =-4(3)-\frac{2}{(3-2{)}^{3}} \\  & =-12-2 \\  & =-14.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=3$ is

$$
m={f}^{′}(3)=-14.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=({x}^{2}-1{)}^{3}+3.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=-1$ is equal to ${f}^{′}(-1).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{d}{dx}\,({x}^{6}-4{x}^{4}+8{x}^{2}-4) \\  & =6{x}^{5}-4(4{x}^{3})+8(2x)-0 \\  & =6{x}^{5}-16{x}^{3}+16x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=-1$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(-1) & =6(-1{)}^{5}-16(-1{)}^{3}+16(-1) \\  & =-6+16-16 \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=-1$ is

$$
m={f}^{′}(-1)=-6.
$$

questions.problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=3{x}^{4}-6{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{x}$ at the point where $x=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=3{x}^{4}-6{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{x}.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=2$ is equal to ${f}^{′}(2).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{4}-6{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{4}-6{x}^{3}+{x}^{-1}) \\  & =4\cdot 3{x}^{3}-3\cdot 6{x}^{2}-{x}^{-2} \\  & =12{x}^{3}-18{x}^{2}-{x}^{-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=2$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(2) & =12(2{)}^{3}-18(2{)}^{2}-(2{)}^{-2} \\  & =96-72-\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{95}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $\frac{95}{4}.$

questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=2{x}^{4}-7{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{x}.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=3$ is equal to ${f}^{′}(3).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{4}-7{x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =2\cdot 4{x}^{3}-7\cdot 3{x}^{2}-6\cdot 2x+{x}^{-2} \\  & =8{x}^{3}-21{x}^{2}-12x+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=3$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(3) & =8({3}^{3})-21({3}^{2})-12(3)+\frac{1}{{3}^{2}} \\  & =216-189-36+\frac{1}{9} \\  & =-9+\frac{1}{9} \\  & =-\frac{80}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=3$ is

$$
m={f}^{′}(3)=-\frac{80}{9}.
$$

questions.problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y={x}^{7}-6{x}^{5}-2670x$ at the point where $x=3.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{7}-6{x}^{5}-2670x.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=3$ is equal to ${f}^{′}(3).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{7}-6{x}^{5}-2670x) \\  & =7{x}^{6}-30{x}^{4}-2670.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=3$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(3) & =7(3{)}^{6}-30(3{)}^{4}-2670 \\  & =5103-2430-2670 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $3.$

questions.problem: What is the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=x-\sqrt[3]{x}$ at the point $(8,6)?$
questions.worked_solution:
This time, we'll use $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ notation. First, we compute the derivative, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x-{x}^{1/3}) \\  & =1-\frac{1}{3}\cdot {x}^{-2/3} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=8$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=8} & =1-\frac{1}{3\sqrt[3]{{8}^{2}}} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{12} \\  & =\frac{11}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $\frac{11}{12}.$

questions.problem: What is the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=5{x}^{4}+\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}$ at the point $(1,6)?$
questions.worked_solution:
This time, we'll use $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ notation. First, we compute the derivative, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5{x}^{4}+\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5{x}^{4}+{x}^{2/3}) \\  & =4\cdot 5{x}^{3}+\frac{2}{3}\cdot {x}^{-1/3} \\  & =20{x}^{3}+\frac{2{x}^{-1/3}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=1$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & =20(1{)}^{3}+\frac{2(1{)}^{-1/3}}{3} \\  & =20+\frac{2}{3} \\  & =\frac{62}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $\frac{62}{3}.$

questions.problem: What is the slope of the tangent to the curve $y={x}^{2}-3x+6\sqrt{x}$ at the point $(4,16)?$
questions.worked_solution:
This time, we'll use $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ notation. First, we compute the derivative, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-3x+6\sqrt{x}) \\  & =2\cdot x-3+\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6{x}^{-1/2} \\  & =2x-3+3{x}^{-1/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=4$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=4} & =2(4)-3+3(4{)}^{-1/2} \\  & =8-3+\frac{3}{2} \\  & =\frac{13}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $\frac{13}{2}.$

questions.problem: Find the positive $x$-coordinate of the point on the curve $y=8{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}-12x-4$ whose tangent has a slope of $6.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=8{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}-12x-4.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to ${f}^{′}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(8{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}-12x-4) \\  & =8\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})-12\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4) \\  & =8\cdot 3{x}^{2}-3\cdot 2x-12\cdot 1-0 \\  & =24{x}^{2}-6x-12.\end{aligned}
$$

We now set ${f}^{′}(x)=6$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}24{x}^{2}-6x-12 & =6 \\ 24{x}^{2}-6x-18 & =0 \\ 6(4{x}^{2}-x-3) & =0 \\ 6(x-1)(4x+3) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent is equal to $6$ at the point where $x=1$ and $x=-\frac{3}{4}.$ Since $x>0$, our answer is $x=1.$

questions.problem: Find the $x$-coordinates of the points on the curve $y=-2{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+20x-1$ whose tangent has a slope of $2.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=-2{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+20x-1.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to ${f}^{′}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2{x}^{3}+6{x}^{2}+20x-1) \\  & =-2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})+6\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})+20\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1) \\  & =-2\cdot 3{x}^{2}+6\cdot 2x+20\cdot 1-0 \\  & =-6{x}^{2}+12x+20.\end{aligned}
$$

We now set ${f}^{′}(x)=2$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-6{x}^{2}+12x+20 & =2 \\ -6{x}^{2}+12x+18 & =0 \\ -6({x}^{2}-2x-3) & =0 \\ -6(x+1)(x-3) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent is equal to $2$ at the points where $x=-1,3.$

questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=2{x}^{2}+4x-3.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to ${f}^{′}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2{x}^{2}+4x-3) \\  & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})+4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =2(2x)+4(1) \\  & =4x+4.\end{aligned}
$$

We now set ${f}^{′}(x)=1$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+4 & =1 \\ 4x & =-3 \\ x & =-\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent is equal to $1$ at the point where $x=-\frac{3}{4}.$

questions.problem: Find the $x$-coordinate of the point on the curve $y={x}^{2}-3x+10$ whose tangent has a slope of $-1.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{2}-3x+10.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to ${f}^{′}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-3x+10) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(10) \\  & =2x-3\cdot 1+0 \\  & =2x-3.\end{aligned}
$$

We now set ${f}^{′}(x)=-1$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-3 & =-1 \\ 2x & =-1+3 \\ 2x & =2 \\ x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent is equal to $-1$ at the point where $x=1.$

questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+14x-6.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to ${f}^{′}(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+14x-6) \\  & =3{x}^{2}+2x+14.\end{aligned}
$$

We now set ${f}^{′}(x)=22$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+2x+14 & =22 \\ 3{x}^{2}+2x-8 & =0 \\ (3x-4)(x+2) & =0 \\ x & =-2,\,\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the positive $x$-coordinate of the points whose tangent has a slope of $6,$ is

$$
x=\frac{4}{3}.
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y = x^2 + \dfrac {1}{x}$ at the point where $x=2.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=x^2+\dfrac 1 x.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=2$ is equal to $f'(2).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+\frac{1}{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+{x}^{-1}) \\  & =2\cdot x-{x}^{-2} \\  & =2x-{x}^{-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=2$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(2) & =2(2)-(2{)}^{-2} \\  & =4-\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{15}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $\dfrac{15}{4}.$

canonical_examples.problem: What is the slope of the tangent to the curve $y = x^4 + 3\sqrt [3]{x^2}$ at the point $(1,4)?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
This time, we'll use $\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d x}$ notation. First, we compute the derivative, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{4}+3\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{4}+3{x}^{2/3}) \\  & =4\cdot {x}^{3}+3\cdot \frac{2}{3}\cdot {x}^{-1/3} \\  & =4{x}^{3}+2{x}^{-1/3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=1$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & =4(1{)}^{3}+2(1{)}^{-1/3} \\  & =4+2 \\  & =6\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $6.$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Point on a Curve With a Certain Slope
canonical_examples.problem: Find the $x$-coordinate of the point on the curve $y=3x^2+1$ where the tangent line has a slope of $-1.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=3x^2+1.$ The slope of the tangent at the point $x$ is equal to $f'(x).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{x}^{2}+1) \\  & =3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1) \\  & =3\cdot 2x+0 \\  & =6x+0 \\  & =6x.\end{aligned}
$$

We now set $f'(x) = -1$ and solve for $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =-1 \\ 6x & =-1 \\ x & =-\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent is equal to $-1$ at the point where $x=-\dfrac 1 6.$
